_source: The H branch of story/data/physics_catalog.json (52 rows, 9 sections), declared 2026-07-31 against research_references/human/PHYSICS_OF_THE_HUMAN.md. Every row id was LOOKED UP in the catalog by name+source, never recalled. H1.02, H2.06, H3.03, H3.07 and H5.02 are already declared in folding.py and are deliberately absent here. 34 of 52 rows declared; the 13 skipped rows are listed in _skipped with the reason, because an unbound row is honest and a guessed signature makes a bad bond look legal.

_skipped.H3.05: Directional gaits. A measured per-direction scaling table (CMU mocap), not an equation; and theHuman publishes it as gait_dir_stride_m / gait_cycles, which are DICTS -- folding.surface() admits only scalars, so it has no binding surface at all. Nothing to declare that would not be my construction.
_skipped.H4.03: Muscle-level metabolic cost. The catalog gives no equation and names two models (Umberger 2003, Bhargava 2004) whose heat-rate partitions differ; choosing one would be inference.
_skipped.H5.01: Pennes bioheat. W/mK arrived in UNITS mid-session from another declarer, but W/m3 for volumetric metabolic heat is still missing; and no membrane publishes a tissue conductivity, a blood perfusion rate or an arterial blood temperature, so every consumed symbol would dock nowhere for a second, unrelated reason.
_skipped.H6.01: Luminous efficiency V(lambda). Needs lm, lm/W and a wavelength axis. UNITS has no photometric unit, and the wavelength axis is unreadable anyway (see _unit_gaps).
_skipped.H6.02: CIE colour matching. Same two blockers as H6.01, plus the tristimulus outputs have no unit in the table.
_skipped.H6.04: Pupil size vs luminance. Watson & Yellott's formula is driven by luminance in cd/m2, which UNITS lacks. Declaring it on age alone would drop its main variable.
_skipped.H6.05: Dark adaptation. Threshold is a luminance (cd/m2); same blocker.
_skipped.H7.03: Tissue water & fat absorption. Produces an absorption coefficient in 1/m, which UNITS lacks; and no membrane publishes a tissue water or fat fraction.
_skipped.H7.04: BSSRDF diffusion dipole. Consumes mu_a and mu_s' in 1/m, which UNITS lacks; theSkin's skin_sss_mfp_mm is a 3-element list, so it is not on any binding surface.
_skipped.H8.03: Grasp closure. A house law with proof D and no equation in the catalog; its inputs could be read as hand geometry OR as the object's size and mass, and choosing between them is exactly the inference this file must not make.
_skipped.H9.01: Gravity field. Proof column is '--'; the row explicitly defers to theSolarSystem/aPlanet upstream. Its law is Newtonian gravitation, which belongs to an E row -- declaring it under an H serial would put a signature on the wrong row.
_skipped.H9.02: Atmospheric pressure/temperature at the body. Proof '--', defers to theAtmosphere. Same reason as H9.01.
_skipped.H9.05: Terrain coupling. Proof '--', defers to theGround/aTerrain/theBiomes. The contact physics it would use is H1.05, declared below.

_unit_gaps: checked against folding.UNITS as it stood on 2026-07-31; W/mK and W/m2K were added by another declarer during this session, so re-check before acting.
1/m -- absorption and scattering coefficients. Blocks H7.03 and H7.04 outright and forces H7.01 to declare a reflectance instead of its native mu_a.
W/m3 -- volumetric metabolic heat (H5.01 Pennes; W/mK is now present, this is the remaining half).
rad/s2 -- angular acceleration, so H1.04's Euler half (tau = I.alpha + omega x I.omega) cannot be written at all.
cd/m2, lm, lm/W, lx -- every photometric quantity. This alone blocks four of the six eye rows (H6.01, H6.02, H6.04, H6.05).

nm -- and worse than missing: '_nm' is currently READ AS NEWTON-METRES. SUFFIX_UNITS carries ('_Nm','N.m'), the exact-case pass finds nothing, and the case-insensitive fallback then matches '_nm'. Confirmed live: unit_of_key('spectrum_nm') and unit_of_key('skin_bands_nm') both return 'N.m'. Every wavelength in theSkin is typed as a torque. Reported, not fixed -- folding.py was being edited by another agent while this file was written.

H1.01.note: de Leva 1996 / Dempster 1955: every segment's mass is a fraction of body mass and every segment's length a fraction of stature, so the whole frame is two numbers plus a measured table. Regime from ANSUR II (6,068 subjects: 46-140 kg, 1.47-2.03 m), widened to cover children and outliers. The stature regime is load-bearing: 'height_m' is a SUBSTRING of 'scale_height_m', which six planetary membranes publish, and without the range a planetary scale height binds happily into a human stature socket.

H1.03.note: AAOS Joint Motion / Kapandji: each joint axis has a measured range of motion, and a pose outside it is not a pose. Ankle plantarflexion 0-50 deg = 0-0.873 rad is the only joint range this tree publishes as a scalar (theAnkle.plantarflex_rad); the rest live in the OpenSim/myobody XML, which is not a story membrane.

H1.04.note: Featherstone 2008. The translational half (F = m.a) and the rotational half (tau = I.alpha + omega x I.omega) need exactly mass and the inertia tensor. Only the translational half is fully writable here: UNITS has no rad/s2, so angular acceleration cannot appear. Inertia regime from de Leva radii of gyration -- a whole leg about the hip is ~1.5-5 kg.m2 for an adult (this tree derives 3.27).

H1.05.note: Signorini 1933 (unilateral contact: gap >= 0 and normal force >= 0) plus Coulomb 1785 (|F_t| <= mu.F_n). The soil's friction coefficient is its angle of repose: mu = tan(phi). Repose regime 20-55 deg spans measured soils and lunar regolith (Carrier, Lunar Sourcebook); this tree's theGround derives 40.03 deg. THE GAP THIS SIGNATURE NAMES: theGround publishes the repose angle but no foot, and theHuman publishes the foot pressure and area but NOT the repose angle it is standing on -- theGround's bearing capacity is carried down to the body as ground_bearing_kPa, its friction angle is not. So the Coulomb half of the contact law cannot be checked at the body.

H2.01.note: Zajac 1989 / Hill 1938: F = F0.(a.f_L.f_V + f_PE).cos(alpha). Pennation regime 0-0.6 rad from Ward et al. 2009 measured cadaveric architecture (0-33 deg across the lower limb). Docks nowhere: the muscles live in myobody, which is a MuJoCo model, not a story membrane -- see _membrane_findings.

H2.02.note: Millard et al. 2013. Both curves are dimensionless multipliers of NORMALISED fibre length and velocity, which is why the units are ratios and the key fragments must be explicit -- an unnormalised length in metres must never reach this socket. Active force-length is non-zero only over l/l0 in [0.44, 1.6]; velocity is normalised by v_max, so -1 is maximal shortening and +1 maximal lengthening.

H2.03.note: Millard 2013 / Thelen 2003: a toe region up to ~2% strain then a linear region, reaching F0 at ~4.9% strain. Above ~8-10% a tendon ruptures, which is where the regime stops. Strain is a ratio and never a length.

H2.04.note: Zajac 1989 / Thelen 2003: a_dot = (u - a)/tau. The time-constant regime is the catalog row's own data column -- tau_act ~ 10 ms, tau_deact ~ 40 ms -- widened to 5-60 ms. This is the one muscle row whose numbers are stated in the catalog itself.

H2.05.note: Ward et al. 2009 measured cadaveric architecture. F0 = PCSA x specific tension, so the peak force of every muscle is an AREA times one shared material constant. Specific tension regime 150-400 kPa brackets the literature band 22.5-35 N/cm2 (225-350 kPa; Zajac uses 250).

H3.01.note: Van Criekinge 2023 (246 adults) + Perry & Burnfield. The cycle partitions: stance is 60-62% of it in normal walking, and double support = 2.(duty - 0.5), which is why duty below 0.5 is a run and not a walk -- that is the regime's floor. theHuman derives duty 0.621 and double support 0.246, both inside the measured band.

H3.02.note: Van Criekinge 2023. The lever is r = tau/F, and the vertical GRF peaks at 1.1-1.2 body weights in normal walking. NO REGIME ON EITHER SYMBOL ON PURPOSE: a moment and a weight are both proportional to g, and this world's g is 7.08 m/s2, so an Earth-calibrated band would reject a correct number. The gravity-INDEPENDENT check is the peak in body weights -- theHuman publishes it as measured_grf_peak_bw = 1.03, but that key carries no unit suffix and is not in units.json, so nothing can bind it. THE GAP THIS SIGNATURE NAMES: theAnkle -- the membrane the catalog assigns this row -- publishes torque_Nm but not a single force in newtons and not a mass, so the lever law cannot close there.

H3.04.note: Winter 1995: dynamic balance is the centre of pressure staying inside the base of support, so the checkable quantity is the margin between the COP excursion and the half-width of the stance. NO REGIME: quiet-stance COP excursion (~1-2 cm) and walking COP travel (~15-25 cm along the foot) are different distributions under one name, and this tree's step width comes from the Van Criekinge measurement itself, so any band I set would be judging their data with my guess. THE GAP: theBalance, the membrane the catalog names, publishes only extent_m, duration_s, declared_by and stub -- it presents no COP and no base of support.

H3.06.note: The Bosco protocol's own equation: h = g.t_flight^2/8, jump height from flight time on a contact mat. NO REGIME on flight time -- it scales as 1/sqrt(g), so an Earth band (0.4-0.7 s for a countermovement jump) would be wrong on any other world. The FORCE half of this row (takeoff and landing peaks in body weights) needs a force-plate trace or a landing stopping distance, and no membrane publishes either; theThrust, the membrane the catalog names, is a 4-key stub.

H3.08.note: Pandolf et al. 1977: M = 1.5W + 2.0(W+L)(L/W)^2 + eta(W+L)(1.5V^2 + 0.35VG). Four inputs, and the fourth is the one nobody publishes -- eta is the TERRAIN coefficient (1.0 blacktop, 1.2 dirt, 1.5 sand), and theGround publishes repose, porosity and bulk density but no Pandolf eta. The walking-speed regime 0.1-3.0 m/s is deliberately generous because the walk-run transition scales with sqrt(gL) and this is not Earth; it still refuses a speed of sound, which is what a speed-shaped socket otherwise grabs.

H4.01.note: Mifflin-St Jeor 1990: BMR(kcal/day) = 10m + 6.25h(cm) - 5(age) + s. Three numbers and a sex term. Resting metabolic rate lands at 60-120 W for an adult, which is the produced band. AGE IS DECLARED EVEN THOUGH IT DOCKS NOWHERE: no membrane in this story publishes a human's age, and three separate rows need one (H4.01, H8.01, H9.04). theSweep -- the membrane the catalog assigns this row -- publishes neither a mass nor a height.

H4.02.note: Ainsworth 2011 Compendium / ISO 8996. One litre of oxygen is ~20.9 kJ of metabolism, so P(W) = 20900.VO2/60 -- theBreath's own numbers satisfy it exactly (0.4773 l/min -> 166.25 W). A MET is defined PER UNIT BODY MASS (3.5 ml.kg-1.min-1), which is why mass is consumed. VO2 regime: resting ~0.25 l/min, elite VO2max ~6 l/min (Wasserman). THE GAP: theBreath publishes the oxygen uptake but not the body mass it is an uptake FOR, so the MET normalisation cannot be checked anywhere.

H4.04.note: Wasserman / ATS-ERS: minute ventilation = tidal volume x breathing frequency, and oxygen uptake follows it through the ventilatory equivalent (VE/VO2 ~ 20-30 at rest). Frequency regime: normal adult resting rate 12-20/min, sustainable maximum ~50-60/min. THE GAP: theBreath -- a PROVEN membrane -- publishes tidal_volume_l = 0.762 and minute_ventilation_l = 11.93, and the product is exactly right, but neither key's unit is readable: '_l' is not in SUFFIX_UNITS and neither key is in units.json, so the law cannot dock to the membrane that implements it.

H4.05.note: Fick 1870: Q = VO2/(Ca - Cv). The arteriovenous oxygen content difference is a volume of O2 per volume of blood, hence a ratio -- ~0.05 (5 ml/100 ml) at rest, 0.15-0.17 at maximal exercise. Nothing publishes it. Related gap: theSkin publishes heart_rate_bpm = 77.3, but '_bpm' is in neither SUFFIX_UNITS nor units.json, so the other route to cardiac output (Q = HR x stroke volume) is unreadable too.

H4.06.note: Hill 1910 / Severinghaus 1979: S = 1/((23400/(P^3 + 150P)) + 1), P in mmHg, P50 = 26.6 mmHg = 0.0355 bar, Hill n ~ 2.7. P50 and n are the law's own constants and are not consumed from a membrane. Regime floor 0.01 bar is below any survivable tissue oxygen tension; ceiling 1.6 bar is the accepted CNS oxygen-toxicity limit for a breathing mix. Binds theBreath, the membrane the catalog names.

H4.07.note: The alveolar route: inspired oxygen partial pressure = F_O2 x (P_ambient - P_H2O), so a thin atmosphere is survivable only by raising the oxygen fraction. The regime floor is PHYSICS, not taste: saturated water vapour at 37 degC is 6.27 kPa = 0.0627 bar, so below that the alveoli are pure water vapour and no gas exchange is possible at all -- the Armstrong limit, which theHuman already tests as above_armstrong_limit. No ceiling declared: nitrogen narcosis and HPNS are physiological limits on the MIX, not on the law. Binds theBreath.

H5.03.note: Villasenor-Mora 2009 measured skin emissivity 0.98 +- 0.01, into Stefan-Boltzmann P = eps.sigma.A.(T_skin^4 - T_surr^4). T IS IN KELVIN AND MUST BE: a fourth power has no meaning on a scale with an arbitrary zero. That is exactly why this signature reports a misfold at aHuman, which publishes T_skin_C = 33.0 in CELSIUS -- the number is right and the socket is not, and the conversion has to be done rather than assumed. Second gap: the measured emissivity 0.98 is 'in repo' per the catalog but no membrane publishes it as a number.

H5.04.note: ISO 9920 + NASA EMU Data Book: the insulation a suit needs is d = k.A.(dT)/Q, and 1 clo = 0.155 m2.K/W. THE TEMPERATURE HERE IS A SPAN AND THE UNIT SAYS SO. THE DEFECT THIS SIGNATURE CATCHES: aHuman publishes dT_defended_K = 26.959, which IS a span (T_skin 33.0 degC minus T_air 6.04 degC), but the '_K' suffix types it as an ABSOLUTE temperature -- 26.96 K is -246 degC. units.json declares dT and dT_equator_pole as 'dK' precisely for this, but the key's own suffix wins over the declaration, so the span is currently typed as an absolute and folding's audit cannot see it (the two keys have different stems, so the inconsistent-pair check never compares them). Metabolic regime 60-900 W: 60-120 W resting (Mifflin-St Jeor), up to ~900 W for the EMU's 2000 Btu/hr ceiling.

H6.03.note: Navarro et al. 1985: the schematic eye is an axial length of ~24.0 mm with a posterior nodal distance of ~16.67 mm, and the retinal image is h = d_nodal x theta. Regimes are the human population ranges (axial 22-26 mm, widened to 20-28). theEye publishes retinal_scale_um_per_deg = 290.9, which is 16.67 mm x pi/180 to four figures -- the law is already implemented there, and this signature is what makes that checkable. ACCOMMODATION IS NOT DECLARED: it is measured in dioptres (1/m), a unit UNITS lacks, so half of this row stays unbindable.

H6.06.note: Sloan / ISO 8596: acuity is the reciprocal of the minimum angle of resolution. 1 arcmin = 2.909e-4 rad = acuity 1.0 (20/20); 10 arcmin = 2.909e-3 rad = 20/200, the legal-blindness threshold, which is where the regime stops. theEye derives 3.106e-4 rad, i.e. slightly worse than 20/20, which is what a real adult measures. Field regimes bracket the standard human extents -- ~200 deg horizontal total and ~130 deg vertical.

H7.01.note: Jacques (OMLC): mu_a of a melanosome goes as lambda^-3.3, so the epidermis is a steep low-pass filter and skin colour is a MEASUREMENT rather than a choice. THE REGIME IS THE CATALOG ROW'S OWN DATA -- 'melanin fractions 1.3-43% by class'; theSkin derives 0.135 and sits inside it. The law's native output is an absorption coefficient in 1/m, a unit UNITS lacks, so what is declared here is the reflectance the membrane actually publishes. The wavelength symbol cannot bind: theSkin publishes spectrum_nm, and '_nm' is currently read as newton-metres.

H7.02.note: Prahl/OMLC compilation (Gratzer + Kollias), 376 rows 250-1000 nm. The dermis absorbs through haemoglobin, and the oxy/deoxy split is what makes flushed skin read differently from cold skin. Blood volume fraction regime 0.1-10% brackets the cutaneous 0.2-7% band; theSkin derives 0.002. The oxygen saturation that selects between the two extinction curves is published by nobody -- H4.06 produces it, and nothing carries it to the skin.

H7.05.note: Zhang & Mak 1999 measured skin-against-material coefficients across nine materials, 0.21-0.61; the regime is widened to 0.1-1.2 for wet and dry extremes. This is the contact law's INPUT, which is why it is a separate row from H1.05: the ground supplies a friction ANGLE and the skin supplies a COEFFICIENT, and they are not the same measurement. Keyed to theGrip's friction_skin_mean_ratio and friction_reference_load_N, both written during this same declaration wave.

H7.06.note: DuBois & DuBois 1916: BSA = 0.007184 . W^0.425 . H^0.725, which lands on 2.01 m2 at the ANSUR median and 2.007 m2 here. THE GAP: theSkin -- the membrane the catalog assigns this row, marked PROVEN -- publishes skin_area_m2 but neither a mass nor a height, so the law that produced its headline number cannot be checked against it. Its stature is present only as the generic extent_m, which no law can find by name without binding to every membrane in the tree.

H8.01.note: Mathiowetz et al. 1985 (n=628, ages 20-94) + the NHANES protocol (8,291 trials in repo, 14,984 people): grip strength is a DISTRIBUTION indexed by age and sex, not a constant. Adult means are ~451 N male and ~265 N female (46 and 27 kgf); NHANES p95 is 546 N, which sets the regime's ceiling. THE GAP: theGrip binds the force but not the age -- it selects a Mathiowetz cell and records the choice only inside the STRING grip_norm_source = 'Mathiowetz 1985 men 30-34'. An age locked in a source string cannot be varied, so no other human can ever be grown from it. Third row blocked on the same missing number (with H4.01 and H9.04).

H8.02.note: Carre et al. 2017 (Wear) + Zhang & Mak 1999. This row is not a single coefficient but a SPAN -- the same hand against soap and against silicone differ by 4x, and it is the span, not the mean, that decides whether a grip is possible. Deliberately a separate binding site from H7.05 so that a wet or gloved coefficient can never bond into a bare-skin socket. theGrip publishes friction_floor_ratio 0.476 and friction_ceiling_ratio 1.26; the regimes bracket a wet smooth glove below 0.1 and a tacky elastomer above 1.5.

H8.04.note: The combined centre of mass is h' = (M.h + L.h_L)/(M + L), and the metabolic penalty follows Pandolf 1977's (W+L)(L/W)^2 term, which is why a badly placed light load costs more than a well placed heavy one. Load regime 0-120 kg: Pandolf is validated to ~70% of body mass, and the NASA EMU is ~127 kg with its PLSS. COM height regime 0.5-1.5 m for an adult standing. theLoad, the membrane the catalog names, is a 4-key stub -- the law binds at theHuman and aHuman instead, which is where suit_mass_kg and com_height_m actually live.

H8.05.note: CMU measured trials + ANSUR sitting and kneeling heights: every posture is the stature times a measured ratio, and the eye height is what the camera actually needs. ANSUR gives eye height/stature ~ 0.936 and sitting height/stature ~ 0.52; theHuman derives 0.925. theStance, the membrane the catalog names, is a 4-key stub. Note also that aHuman -- the SUITED human, the one that most needs a camera height -- republishes stature but drops eye_height_m.

H9.03.note: NASA EMU Data Book Rev V: a suit is a mass you carry (EMU ~47 kg, ~127 kg with the PLSS) and a pressure you breathe (EMU 0.296 bar = 4.3 psi, which is what forces the prebreathe). Only the mass half is declared as consumed, because it is the half that closes in this tree -- theHuman publishes suit_weight_N = 70.156 N = 9.9145 kg x 7.0761 m/s2 exactly. The pressure half lives one membrane away as theBreath.P_loop_bar, and no single membrane presents both, so the suited human's mass and its loop pressure cannot be checked together.

H9.04.note: WHO/CDC growth standards + ANSUR II male and female + gait-by-decade, all in repo. This is the row that makes A human out of THE human, and every one of its outputs is a distribution over one number nobody publishes. Third and final row blocked on the same missing key: there is no age anywhere in this story.

_membrane_findings.myobody: H1.03 (partly), H2.01-H2.06 -- six rows -- name 'myobody' as their membrane. THERE IS NO myobody MEMBRANE: folding.membranes() finds 42 numbers.json in story/, and none of them is myobody. It is a MuJoCo model (ChimeraEngine/vendor/myo_sim), so the entire actuation section of the human catalog is assigned to something outside the story tree and can never dock until myobody publishes a numbers.json.
_membrane_findings.stubs: theBalance, theHand, theLoad, theStance and theThrust each still publish exactly four keys (declared_by, duration_s, extent_m, stub=true). Six H rows name one of them (H3.04, H3.06, H3.08, H8.03, H8.04, H8.05) and none can dock. theEye and theGrip were 4-key stubs when this file was started and were written by other agents during the same wave -- H6.03, H6.06, H7.05, H8.01 and H8.02 were re-keyed to what they actually publish, so those key fragments are the youngest and most likely to churn.
_membrane_findings.theEye_unit_defects: written during this wave and worth catching before it hardens: adapting_luminance_cd_m2 = 5885.8, luminance_max_cd_m2 = 1e8 and luminance_min_cd_m2 = 1e-6 are all read as AREAS in m2, because '_m2' is the suffix that matches and cd/m2 is not in UNITS; luminous_efficacy_lm_per_W = 93.0 and efficacy_at_solar_reference_lm_per_W are read as WATTS; photopic_peak_nm = 555.1 and scotopic_peak_nm = 506.5 are read as NEWTON-METRES (the '_nm' collision); saccade_peak_velocity_deg_s = 397.7 is a RATE read as a duration in seconds; ipd_sample_n = 4082 is a COUNT read as NEWTONS; and cone_nyquist_cyc_per_deg, diffraction_cutoff_cyc_per_deg, render_px_per_deg and retinal_scale_um_per_deg are all per-degree quantities read as plain DEGREES. None of these is caught by folding.audit, because m2, W, N and deg all permit the values they hold.
_membrane_findings.theAnkle: publishes 27 keys in J, W, N.m, N.m/kg, m, rad, s, ratio, frac and count -- but no mass and no force. Any law needing a newton or a kilogram is refused there by construction.
_membrane_findings.theSkin: publishes skin_area_m2 but no mass and no height, so H7.06 (the law that produced that number) cannot dock to it.
_membrane_findings.theSweep: publishes no mass, no height and no VO2, so H4.01 and H4.02 -- both assigned to it -- cannot dock.
_live_unit_defects_found_while_declaring: aHuman.dT_defended_K = 26.959 -- a SPAN (33.0 degC skin minus 6.04 degC air) typed by its '_K' suffix as an ABSOLUTE temperature, i.e. -246 degC. units.json declares dT and dT_equator_pole as 'dK' for exactly this reason, but a key's own suffix wins over the declaration. folding's inconsistent-pair audit cannot see it because nothing else shares the stem. H5.04 above catches it.

theHuman.cadence_steps_s = 1.6871 -- a RATE (steps per second; it is exactly 1/step_time_s and cadence_steps_min/60) typed by its '_s' suffix as a DURATION. Dimensionally inverted: T^-1 published as T^1. The audit's inconsistent-pair check misses it because _stem() reads 'cadence_steps_min' through the '_steps_min' rule (stem 'cadence') and 'cadence_steps_s' through the '_s' rule (stem 'cadence_steps'), so the two are never compared.

unreadable units on real numbers: theBreath.tidal_volume_l (litres) and theBreath.minute_ventilation_l (litres/min) -- '_l' is in neither SUFFIX_UNITS nor units.json, and their product is exactly right, so a PROVEN law is invisible; theSkin.heart_rate_bpm (1/min); theHuman.measured_grf_peak_bw and grf_peak_bw_typed_was (the only gravity-independent check H3.02 has).
